top.title: Has Derrick Henry played his last game as a Raven? Making sense of trade rumors around star RB
top.description: Has Derrick Henry played his last game as a Raven? Making sense of trade rumors around star RB originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Ravens , once 4-1 and near the top of the AFC, are in serious trouble after four consecutive losses. Not only is Baltimore last in the AFC North at 4-5, but the Ravens might not have Lamar Jackson back on the field this season after thumb surgery. Help is on the way, as veteran Jacoby Brissett is coming over from the Cardinals in a trade to take over at quarterback, but it might take a heroic effort for Baltimore to turn its season around. With the trade deadline approaching on Tuesday, would the Ravens consider trading future Hall of Fame RB Derrick Henry? Here's what you need to know about the rumors surrounding Henry. MORE: Can Ravens still make the playoffs? Has Derrick Henry played his last game as a Raven? The future of Henry is something to "keep half an eye on," ESPN's Dan Graziano reported before the Ravens' loss to the Jaguars . "Henry is turning 33 in January. He is scheduled to earn $12 million next year, and none of that money is guaranteed," Graziano said. "If he isn't in Baltimore's plans beyond this year, the Ravens could find themselves fielding offers over the next week." Fielding offers isn't the same as shopping a player, but as the math becomes more difficult for the Ravens in the AFC, Graziano lists a handful of reasons why a trade could make sense, from Henry's age and contract to the reality of trying to win without Jackson. The number of contenders in need of a running back could also get the Ravens some value in a trade. Several teams, including the Giants , Broncos , Bengals , Vikings and Packers , have been reported as suitors for Indianapolis' Jonathan Taylor. Only one of them can get him. Could the losers of that sweepstakes make a play for Henry? Teams being interested in Henry is no surprise. The Ravens willingly talking about deals involving Henry is a separate subject, and to this point, no reports have indicated they are looking to deal their running back. With Brissett coming in and a more favorable portion of the schedule ahead, one would think Baltimore still has visions of competing this season. If the Ravens wanted to get something for Henry, though, the best time might be right now. top.title: Terrorists abduct 10 in Ogun, demand 25m ransom
top.description: By Adeola Badru Families of 10 travellers, including a former member of the National Youth Service Corps NYSC, Olusoji Adedapo, have raised the alarm over their abduction at Ijebu Awa, a boundary community between Ogun and Oyo states, with the kidnappers demanding N25 million for their release. Although unconfirmed reports indicated that some of the passengers were serving corps members, the police said none of those abducted was a corps member. The 24-year-old Adedapo, reportedly completed his national service in Edo State last week and was travelling to Ibadan when the incident occurred on Tuesday. His cousin, Adeseye Timilehin, who disclosed this, said the family had been thrown into distress, particularly as the kidnappers had issued a 24-hour deadline for payment of the ransom. He explained that Dapo (Adedapo) had been updating the family about his journey until he sent a video showing the traffic situation on the road, which turned out to be their last communication. Timilehin said the family learnt of the abduction shortly after 7pm on Tuesday, when one of the passengers reportedly escaped and contacted another family member. He explained that Dapo was travelling with a friend, Tunde, with whom he had served during the NYSC programme, informing that Tunde was the only passenger who managed to escape the attack and alerted the family. According to him: “On Tuesday morning, my cousin left Benin City, Edo State. He was posted to Edo State for NYSC and did his Passing-Out Ceremony last week. So, he was on his way back to Ibadan. “He was still giving us updates about his journey. At some point, he posted that there was traffic in Benin. I have the videos of the traffic jam on my phone. By the time they were able to get out of the traffic, it was already 3pm. “They kept telling the driver that it was already late and that they should return to Benin and continue the journey the following day, but the driver insisted on going. By the time they got to Ijebu at about 7pm, they were attacked by the bandits.” He noted d that Tunde told him the driver had swerved into the bush and stopped immediately after the gunmen appeared in front of the vehicle, forcing the passengers to flee for safety. “He told me that when the driver swerved into the bush and stopped, the bandits immediately jumped in front of their bus. He had to hide in the bush while the rest ran for safety and were captured. He was able to escape, but my brother and the others were taken away,” he said. Timilehin said the family subsequently established contact with Tunde, who provided further details of the incident and confirmed that police officers had arrived at the scene, rescued him and taken him to a police station, where he spent the night. top.description: The 3 main reasons behind the Magic's slow start to 2026-27 season originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Sean Sweeney era in Orlando could be off to a better start. The Magic dropped their third straight game on Thursday night, a 117-104 defeat against the Phoenix Suns despite a 27-point performance from Wendell Carter Jr. The loss dropped Orlando to 2-6 so far this season. For a team with playoff expectations, the Magic have dug themselves an early hole to climb out of — the path to the playoffs will not be easy, particularly if a few areas of concern aren't addressed. Here's a look at the three main reasons for the Magic's slow start in 2026-27. Reasons behind the Magic's slow start Injuries To put it plainly: the Magic are a much better team when Paolo Banchero is on the floor. That's no knock on Orlando — most NBA teams struggle without their best player. But after a 35-point night in the season-opener, Banchero has been out with a sprained ankle. Without Banchero, the Magic haven't had a go-to scorer, especially with Franz Wagner (41.9% from the floor) struggling to shoot the ball early this season. Orlando hasn't had a 30-point scorer since Banchero's opener against Atlanta, and it took 28 Desmond Bane points to beat the Raptors last week. Banchero was given a four-to-six week timeline, meaning the Magic still likely have plenty of time without him. And that's all without mentioning Jalen Suggs' absence, leaving an all-around impact on both ends of the floor vacant. Orlando needs Wagner to be more efficient as a three-level scorer, and for Bane to take over offensively more often. Without Banchero and Suggs, there are critical voids not being filled. Turnovers Entering Thursday's game, the Magic were averaging the sixth-most turnovers per game in the NBA, in the same territory as teams like the Nets , Bulls , Kings , Pelicans and Jazz . That isn't a group of teams Orlando expected to be in conversations with this season. That was before another 25 turnovers against the Suns, who came into the game with just one win this season. Wagner turned the ball over six times — though he did have 15 assists — and Anthony Black had another five turnovers. Particularly with Banchero and Suggs absent, the margin for error is thinner. The Magic need Wagner to take care of the ball as the lead star right now, and Sweeney's first Orlando team needs to play a much cleaner brand of basketball if it's going to turn things around. top.title: High School Coach Refuses to Apologize For Winning
top.description: Westlake head coach Rick Clausen directs his players during a practice on Aug. 11, 2026, at Westlake High. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Rick Clausen is not backing down from the parents who hired private investigators to dig into his Westlake High School program. The coach told the California Post on Thursday that he has zero intention of saying sorry for fixing a team that went 0-10 in 2024. He called the letter from “Concerned Westlake High School Parents” comical and stated that nothing shocks him in today’s society. This is a clear line in the sand for a coach who turned a floundering squad into a 7-3 playoff team in just two years. The parents sent a five-paragraph letter to the school on October 28. They claimed they were under the direction of legal counsel and had signed a contract with a private investigation company. The letter accused the program of using financial inducements to bring in players for football reasons. They said they were investigating whether residency and transfer information accurately reflected the students’ actual circumstances. The group even cited CIF Bylaw 510, which bans undue influence for athletic purposes in public schools. The Turnaround That Sparked Anger Westlake High School went from a winless season to a 10-1 record in Clausen’s first year. The team is now 7-3 and earned a spot in the playoffs after going 3-2 in their conference. He told the New York Post that he has inherited programs down on their luck before and turned them around. He said he will not apologize for doing what is needed to win. The coach believes that competition is a foreign concept for some families. He told reporters that some kids and families feel entitled to certain things. He said that mindset belongs to the old Westlake and does not align with the program’s direction going forward. Clausen added that everything in his program is earned through competition. He declared he would not apologize for constructing a program based on good families and good kids with college goals. Parents Feel Entitled To Playing Time Social media critics suggest the letter came from parents upset about their children not getting playing time. According to the letter, parents will file a formal request with the CIF Southern Section to investigate suspected recruiting violations. They claimed to have information that certain student-athletes had been approached about transferring for football reasons. No response was received after the school was contacted for comment. top.title: Arch Manning and Texas get more bad news
top.description: Oct 10, 2026; Dallas, Texas, USA; Texas Longhorns quarterback Arch Manning (16) looks on before the game between the Sooners and the Longhorns at Cotton Bowl. Mandatory Credit: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Arch Manning and the Texas Longhorns have won back-to-back games to get their season back on track, but they’ve been piling up injuries along the way. Texas already lost star left tackle Trevor Goosby for the season last month, and several other key players are banged up heading into Saturday’s road game against Missouri. Now, the Longhorns have been dealt another significant blow as running back Hollywood Smothers, who opened the season as Texas’ starter, will reportedly miss the rest of the year with a torn MCL, leaving an already struggling rushing attack even thinner. Texas’ Injury Woes Manning entered the season as a Heisman Trophy favorite, but back-to-back 27-24 losses to Oklahoma and Florida put him at risk of being benched. Head coach Steve Sarkisian even warned Manning that he would make a change if things didn’t improve. Texas responded with a 34-27 win over then-No. 7 Ole Miss on Oct. 24, but a key player went down during the game as Goosby was carted off in the first half with a knee injury and was later ruled out for the season , taking away the player responsible for protecting Manning’s blind side. Goosby, a preseason first-team All-American, is widely considered the top left tackle prospect in the upcoming NFL Draft. Texas was already shorthanded in that game, playing without pass rusher Colin Simmons and Smothers. Star wide receiver Cam Coleman also left the game with an injury. The Longhorns followed that up with a 31-3 win over Mississippi State last Saturday, as Manning threw three touchdown passes. But the offensive line issues were obvious, as Manning was sacked six times, and Coleman left early for the second consecutive game. “I think we still have better football out there that we have to go out and play,” Sarkisian said after the win, via the Associated Press . Smothers Out for Season On Thursday, Manning and the Longhorns got even more bad news this season, as On3’s Pete Nakos reported that Smothers will miss the remainder of the season. top.title: Slick Jaguars breeze past rudderless Ravens 33-10
top.description: Trevor Lawrence of the Jacksonville Jaguars threw for 242 yards and a touchdown pass (Patrick Smith) Trevor Lawrence guided the Jacksonville Jaguars to a straightforward 33-10 victory Thursday over a desperate Baltimore Ravens team forced to rely on its ailing third-string quarterback. Lawrence threw for 242 yards and a touchdown pass to Parker Washington, with Bhayshul Tuten running for a touchdown on the game's first drive and fellow Jaguars back Chris Rodriguez Jr. sealing victory on a dismal rainy night for Baltimore fans. Deprived of their talismanic quarterback Lamar Jackson and his backup Tyler Huntley due to injuries, Baltimore handed a first NFL start to undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who played with enormous heavy strapping on his own injured ankle throughout. Fagnano battled gamely but there was little he could do to prevent the slick Jaguars from moving to 6-2. Having now won 14 of their last 16 regular-season games, Jacksonville's latest win further burnished their credentials as dark horses in the race for the NFL championship. "We've come together, I think we've got a great group that's all on the same page. We all think similarly. A bunch of hard workers," said Lawrence. "Everybody's gelling...You're seeing it come to life." The closing stages of a fourth straight loss for the Ravens -- who sank to 4-5 -- played out in front of emptying stands at the M&T Bank Stadium. Baltimore are already pinning their slim hopes of a playoff run on the expected arrival this weekend of veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett. Lawrence began the night driving the Jaguars swiftly into the red zone with a 52-yard pass to rookie tight end Nate Boerkircher, before Tuten dashed across the line. The Ravens offense tried every trick in the book to protect their novice quarterback, with star running back Derrick Henry taking multiple direct snaps in wildcat formation. It yielded little, though Henry did move into 7th place in all-time NFL rushing yards, surpassing LaDainian Tomlinson. In the second quarter Lawrence sprang back to life with two superb passes, the first finding tight end Brenton Strange for a first down, before the second sent Washington 50 yards into the end zone. After a series of field goals, Rodriguez ran in a touchdown from a direct snap to make it 33-3. Baltimore's Justice Hill sprinted for a 65-yard touchdown to restore some pride with a late score. amz/sla

top.title: Jones - the smiling wind-up artist who refuses to fade away
top.description: Eddie Jones has coached in Australia, England, Japan and South Africa [Getty Images] An Eddie Jones press conference has always been an event in itself. You never quite know what's coming. A compliment, a cutting observation, a verbal grenade. Sometimes all three, invariably delivered with that mischievous smile. Jones belongs to a disappearing generation of coaches who understood that the contest could begin long before the players took the field. Warren Gatland could intimidate with his imposing presence and gruff demeanour alone. Jose Mourinho proclaimed himself 'The Special One' and made confrontation an art form. Jones was different. Small in stature, with an almost permanent grin, he could stir up an entire nation while thoroughly enjoying himself. All three built reputations on dominance. Not simply on the pitch, but over the agenda, their players and the organisations they represented. But the language of coaching is changing. Wales head coach Steve Tandy talks about connection and relationships. Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler emphasises collaboration, trust and understanding the person behind the player. Neither lacks ambition or authority, but their approach contrasts with the era of the all-powerful head coach. At 66, Jones remains one of rugby's most fascinating characters from that old school. The method behind the mischief In 2018 Jones questioned whether Wales fly-half Rhys Patchell could handle the pressure of playing England at Twickenham, while describing Warren Gatland's team as "confident and cocky". But his provocations sometimes crossed the line. That same year Jones apologised after footage emerged of him using some choice language to describe Wales and Ireland in less than flattering terms at a sponsors' event the previous year. The former was classic Jones. Identify a weakness, plant a seed of doubt and ensure everyone was talking about it. The latter showed when the wind-ups went too far. But how much was calculated? Speaking to BBC Sport prior to Japan's Nations Championship meeting with Wales, Jones offered an intriguing explanation. "Some of them were planned to an extent. Others might have come out of the press conference. Sometimes you say things at the press conference that you don't mean to say. But, yeah, sometimes." Players picked on form not club location - Tandy Jones looks to create Japan history in Cardiff Then came a surprising admission. "And particularly with England, I always felt with the English that they didn't have enough confidence in themselves." England? Lacking confidence? Jones explained that part of his responsibility was to provide that self-belief. "So I felt one of my roles was to give them that confidence, to be almost the battering ram for them." He explained that Dapo (Adedapo) had been updating the family about his journey until he sent a video showing the traffic situation on the road, which turned out to be their last communication. Timilehin said the family learnt of the abduction shortly after 7pm on Tuesday, when one of the passengers reportedly escaped and contacted another family member. So, he was on his way back to Ibadan. “He was still giving us updates about his journey. At some point, he posted that there was traffic in Benin. I have the videos of the traffic jam on my phone. By the time they were able to get out of the traffic, it was already 3pm. “They kept telling the driver that it was already late and that they should return to Benin and continue the journey the following day, but the driver insisted on going. By the time they got to Ijebu at about 7pm, they were attacked by the bandits.” He noted d that Tunde told him the driver had swerved into the bush and stopped immediately after the gunmen appeared in front of the vehicle, forcing the passengers to flee for safety. “He told me that when the driver swerved into the bush and stopped, the bandits immediately jumped in front of their bus. nigeria.title: Atiku Verdict: APC wants opposition fighting – Ameh
nigeria.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — High Chief Peter Ameh, the National Democratic Congress (NDC) senatorial candidate for Kogi East, has warned opposition parties against celebrating the court judgment that sacked the David Mark-led National Working Committee of the African Democratic Congress (ADC) and nullified Atiku Abubakar’s candidacy. Ameh said the ruling should not be seen as a victory for any political camp, warning that the All Progressives Congress (APC) stood to benefit from divisions within the opposition. He spoke in Abuja on Thursday, urging opposition parties to resist attempts to turn the judgment into an opportunity for political infighting. According to him, the APC would be comfortable with any opposition party being weakened, regardless of the party’s identity or political affiliation. “The APC, which is the ultimate beneficiary of this judgment, will be happy keeping any party in the opposition weakened. They do not care which party logo you wave. They want us fighting each other so we never notice the real game being played against all of us,” he said. Ameh cautioned that what might appear to be a victory for one faction today could become a tool against another political group tomorrow. “Before anyone starts dancing, remember: today’s victory for one camp is tomorrow’s weapon against another. The same forces that can erase one candidate or one leadership structure can just as easily turn on yours when it becomes convenient. Political affiliation is not a shield,” he said. He added: “Stay alert. This is not a win for any side. It is a warning.” The NDC candidate urged opposition parties to channel their energy towards demanding free, fair and credible elections, rather than engaging in disputes over political leadership and candidacies. He also criticised the APC-led administration, accusing it of failing to deliver good governance to Nigerians over the past 11 years. “For 11 years, this APC government has failed to provide good governance to Nigerians. nigeria.title: UN, EU, Germany woo investors to Borno
nigeria.description: …Zulum pledges business-friendly reforms By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The United Nations (UN), European Union (EU), German Government and other development partners are supporting efforts to attract private investment to Borno State to create jobs and help displaced families rebuild their livelihoods. At the third Borno State Private Sector Engagement and Investment Roundtable in Abuja on Thursday, representatives of the UN, EU and German Embassy pledged continued support for the state’s recovery through private sector investment. The Governor Babagana Zulum-led administration initiated the roundtable series with a meeting in Lagos, focusing on financing bankable projects and supporting small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). The second edition was held in Kano, with emphasis on agriculture, livestock, fisheries and infrastructure. More than 50 prospective investors attended the Abuja roundtable. The representative of the UN Resident Coordinator’s Office in Nigeria, Thembekile Dube-Nanbe, urged development partners to translate the investment initiative into concrete action. “Let us identify viable investment opportunities, mobilise capital, establish lasting partnerships, and commit to measurable results,” Dube-Nanbe said. The EU Head of Human Development, Laila Ben Amor Mathieu, said the Union had supported Borno through its most difficult years by providing humanitarian assistance and backing stabilisation and recovery efforts. “Grants and public budgets alone will not finance recovery at the scale Borno needs. Private capital must play its part, and the role of us partners is to make that possible,” Mathieu said. She said investors could support the proposed Borno State Durable Solutions Trust Fund or pursue commercially viable projects backed by incentives, including access to land, industrial hubs and tax measures. Mathieu urged businesses to identify projects for further consideration, partner with local companies and create opportunities for women and young people. “Borno is becoming an investment story. The European Union is proud to be part of it,” she said. The Head of Development Cooperation at the German Embassy, Dr Karen Jansen, commended Governor Zulum for restoring communities, rebuilding infrastructure and public services, and opening the state’s economy to investors. She urged investors to sustain their commitments as the economy grows, assuring the state of Germany’s continued support. “Mobilising private sector investment, including through blended finance, will be essential to complement development cooperation and support Borno’s sustainable reconstruction,” Jansen said. Governor Zulum, who was represented by his Chief of Staff, Dr Babagana Mustapha Mallumbe, urged private investors to take advantage of business opportunities in the state, assuring them of government support and simpler administrative procedures. nigeria.title: Benue SEMA raises alarm over rising snakebites, treats two IDPs
nigeria.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Benue State Emergency Management Agency (SEMA) has expressed concern over rising cases of snakebites across the state, warning that the incidents are increasingly affecting farmers, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and other vulnerable residents. The concern followed two recent snakebite incidents involving a 35-year-old man, Isaac Shula, and a 19-year-old girl, Mbapuun Tyoshio, both residents of Daudu 1 IDP camp in Guma Local Government Area of the state. The victims were reportedly bitten by snakes while working on their farms and have since been referred to the Benue State University Teaching Hospital (BSUTH), Makurdi, where they are receiving medical attention under the care of Benue SEMA. The agency’s Health Focal Person, Dr Amos Dzungwe, said snakebite cases had continued to increase across the state, affecting not only displaced persons but also farmers and other vulnerable populations. He said the agency had received numerous requests for medical intervention from different parts of the state, reflecting growing concern over the incidents. According to him, two snakebite patients were successfully discharged within the last two weeks, while others remained on admission and were receiving treatment. Dzungwe warned against delays in seeking medical attention, stressing that late presentation at health facilities could result in severe complications and poor health outcomes. He urged members of the public to seek immediate medical attention at appropriate health facilities whenever snakebite incidents occur. Meanwhile, Benue SEMA has urged the public to disregard what it described as misleading reports and politically motivated narratives surrounding snakebite incidents in the state, particularly those involving IDPs. The agency maintained that health emergencies and the lives of vulnerable citizens should not be subjected to political manipulation. It reaffirmed its commitment to providing timely medical assistance to snakebite victims and others affected by emergencies, irrespective of their status or location. nigeria.title: Soludo seeks partnership with pharmacists to strengthen healthcare
nigeria.description: By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA — Anambra State Governor, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has called for a strategic partnership between the state government and the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria (PSN) to strengthen the healthcare system and improve access to quality pharmaceutical services. Soludo made the call on Wednesday while declaring open the ongoing four-day 99th Annual National Delegate Conference of the society in Awka, stressing that pharmacists played a critical role in building an effective healthcare system. Describing the gathering, tagged ‘Ijele 2026’, as historic, the governor said his administration had prioritised human capital development, education and healthcare. He cited the introduction of free education from kindergarten to Senior Secondary School Three (SS3), as well as free antenatal care in government hospitals, as part of his administration’s interventions in the sectors. Soludo also said his government had revamped the state’s primary healthcare system, disclosing that more than 250,000 expectant mothers had benefited from zero-cost antenatal care, while over 950 free Caesarean Section operations had been performed. “To further solidify Anambra’s position as the nation’s premier pharma hub, let me also inform you that work on the development of the state-of-the-art Pharmaceutical Hub in Oba, alongside the upcoming Coordinated Wholesale Centre slated for delivery early next year, is currently ongoing in the state,” he said. The governor urged the PSN leadership to work closely with the state government to enforce safety standards in pharmaceutical operations and tackle the circulation of counterfeit drugs. He also challenged the society to address unethical practices within the profession, particularly the activities of illegal drug outlets operating under the guise of licensed pharmacies. The projects, comprising two interconnected and 35 isolated mini-grids, are expected to connect 125,106 households across Gummi, Gusau, Kaura Namoda, Maradun, Shinkafi, Tsafe and Zurmi Local Government Areas. The integrated capacity-building programme, implemented through the National Malaria Elimination Programme (NMEP) and the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, was inaugurated at Mokland Hotel, Ibara, GRA, Abeokuta, Ogun State. Speaking at the event, Consultant Medical Parasitologist, College of Medicine, University of Lagos, Professor Wellington Oyibo, said accurate diagnosis was critical to effective treatment, warning that laboratory personnel must be equipped to identify different malaria parasite species and distinguish infections from other illnesses. He said microscopy remained essential despite the availability of rapid diagnostic tests and molecular technologies, stressing the need for quality assurance, proper documentation and timely reporting. nigeria.title: Bournemouth stay perfect in Europa League as Milan lose again
nigeria.description: Bournemouth extended their perfect Europa League record on Thursday as they came from behind to win 3-1 at 10-man Sparta Prague, while Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan suffered a third defeat in four matches. Gambian Ebrima Singhateh ran from his own half to score a fine individual goal as Sparta took the lead in the Czech Republic after Bournemouth midfielder Lewis Cook hit the post with a first-half penalty. Sparta had Tobias Guddal sent off before half-time and Bournemouth equalised through Tyler Adams on 57 minutes. Evanilson steered the Cherries ahead nine minutes from time and Rayan bagged a late third as Bournemouth’s substitutes sent the European newcomers top of the table with a fourth successive victory. Marco Rose’s side have won each of their past seven matches in all competitions ahead of a Premier League trip to Ipswich this weekend. “It’s a big achievement and we have to continue, we need to stay alert, sharp,” Rose told TNT Sports. “It’s up to us to use this momentum. Everyone tries to beat us, if we get in a comfort zone just a little bit we get in trouble.” Milan lost 2-0 at home to Ferencvaros as the Hungarians kept pace with Bournemouth, maintaining their 100 percent record in Europe. Haiti international Lenny Joseph struck twice in the second half at San Siro to earn Ferencvaros a deserved win over the seven-time European champions despite having Bamidele Yusuf sent off. “We gifted opportunities, made stupid errors. We were not prepared to play football tonight,” Amorim told Sky Sport. “I don’t want to lie to my players. We cannot play like this in front of our own fans. It was a very poor performance.” Milan are languishing outside the top 24 with just three points at the halfway stage of the league phase. “I won’t give up on this competition. As long as we’re not mathematically out of it, we’ll keep fighting,” Amorim added. Crystal Palace snatched a 1-1 draw at home to Hoffenheim as Japanese midfielder Daichi Kamada levelled in stoppage time. Alexander Prass gave Hoffenheim an early lead at Selhurst Park and Palace lost Adam Wharton to a second yellow card before Kamada rescued a point for Pierre Sage’s struggling side. Palace, last season’s UEFA Conference League winners, have five points from four outings in the Europa League but sit in the Premier League’s relegation zone, just behind Manchester United on goal difference. nigeria.title: Ebola patient flown to UK from DR Congo
nigeria.description: A UK medic who tested positive for Ebola while working on the outbreak of the disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been flown to London for treatment, the government said Thursday. The unnamed British citizen “has returned to the UK for specialist treatment after testing positive for the disease”, the government said in a statement. Africa’s latest Ebola outbreak has killed more than 5,300 people, the vast majority of them in the Democratic Republic of Congo, according to the continent’s top health agency. The British government said that the UK medic is now being treated at the Royal Free Hospital in London. This hospital has a high-level isolation unit “specifically designed for this purpose” and strict protocols to prevent contact with the general public, it said. Renu Bindra, deputy director of the all hazards public health response team at the UK health security agency (UKHSA) said “the risk to the wider public remains low”. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, Oshiomhole described Obi as a trader whose approach, according to him, focuses on short-term gains rather than long-term national development. “Peter Obi has not offered any alternative. I think it is you or someone else who asked him for security, what will you do differently? He said, it’s in his heart. “I’ve always said that Peter Obi is a trader; the logic of a trader is short term turnover. A statesman that Tinubu represents thinks of the next generation,” he said. ﻿ Oshiomhole said he respected the right of opposition candidates to contest for the presidency but believed Tinubu should remain in office after “having gone through all the teething problems” rather than “recruit a new apprentice.” He also criticised the record of the administration of former President Olusegun Obasanjo, under which former Vice President Atiku Abubakar served, alleging that they were unable to guarantee the payment of workers’ salaries. The Edo North Senator said the 2027 presidential election would present Nigerians with a choice between Tinubu, whom he credited with unifying the exchange rate, and Atiku, whose administration he accused of allowing different exchange rates for people based on their connections. Oshiomhole also defended the Tinubu administration’s handling of workers’ welfare, saying the Federal Government’s approval of a ₦70,000 transport allowance showed that the President cared about them. “I think this government is doing well. nigeria.title: Italian chef sacked for refusing to put pineapple on pizza, says it insulted his culture
nigeria.description: An Italian chef in Australia has lost an unfair dismissal claim after being sacked for, among other workplace issues, refusing to serve ham and pineapple pizza, describing the topping as an insult to his culture. Davide Tamburella was dismissed from the now-closed La Costa restaurant in Brisbane in May, following a meeting with management over several complaints about his conduct. One of the issues raised was his refusal to prepare ham and pineapple pizzas for guests attending an event at the restaurant. According to a ruling by Australia’s Fair Work Commission, Tamburella argued that instructions from management “need not be followed when it is offensive to his culture”. The commission noted that the chef’s objection to the fruit was because “he considers, as an Italian, that putting pineapple on a pizza is an insult to his culture”. It also found that this was not the first time he had refused to use pineapple on pizzas, recording three such instances over four years. On a previous occasion, Tamburella had asked his employer to “check how important it is for Italians not to put pineapple on a pizza”. Beyond the dispute over pizza toppings, management raised concerns about his use of foul language, communication style and what it described as an “escalation of frustration in the workplace”. The ruling also detailed an incident in April when Tamburella fractured bones in his right hand after striking a metal handrail at work. The chef had reportedly hoped to secure employer sponsorship for a visa that would allow him to remain in Australia as a permanent resident. However, following his dismissal, the restaurant discontinued the sponsorship process. Tamburella subsequently approached the Fair Work Commission, challenging his dismissal. However, the commission rejected his unfair dismissal claim because it was lodged outside the permitted timeframe. The restaurant’s managing director, Elliot Ingram, told the Daily Mail there was “more to this story than a pizza topping”. The BBC said it had contacted Tamburella for comment. On his LinkedIn profile, the chef describes himself as someone whose career has focused on “delivering exceptional food” and “improving business performance”. He also shared a post titled “letter for chefs” three months ago, centred on the theme of “respecting the ingredients”. His LinkedIn profile indicates that he now works at another restaurant in Brisbane. A BBC check found that pineapple is not included on its menu. Meanwhile, Queensland, where the restaurant was located, is regarded as Australia’s pineapple heartland and produces the country’s commercially grown pineapples. The state is also home to the Big Pineapple, a 16-metre fibreglass structure on the Sunshine Coast that has become a popular local landmark. world.title: 'Leaders all over the world understand that Trump is only there for two more years & then he's gone'
world.description: In American politics, the possession of presidential power does not necessarily guarantee the capacity to exercise it. Few contemporary leaders have embodied this contradiction as dramatically as Donald Trump. Following what political scientist Ian Bremmer describes as the most consequential electoral reversal for a governing party in more than half a century, the founder of Eurasia Group and GZERO Media argues that the United States has entered a new political phase: the beginning of the end of Trump's capacity to dominate the domestic and international agenda. In this wide-ranging interview with France 24, Bremmer revisits his provocative thesis that America has already reached "peak Trump." Far from suggesting that the president has become powerless, he contends that his authority is increasingly constrained by congressional opposition, Republican discontent, unpopular foreign policy decisions and the growing awareness among international leaders that the present administration has a limited political horizon. The historical reversal is, in Bremmer's account, extraordinary: "Trump back in 2024 engineered for himself the biggest political comeback in American political history. And now, only two years later, the biggest loss in 50 years." At the heart of his analysis lies a fundamental distinction between institutional authority and political influence. Trump remains commander-in-chief, retains the instruments of executive government and continues to command extraordinary media attention. Yet Bremmer argues that the president's ability to translate those advantages into effective political outcomes is diminishing. The consequences, he suggests, extend far beyond Washington. From the war in Iran and the unresolved conflict in Ukraine to the future of transatlantic relations, America's allies and adversaries are beginning to adjust their strategic calculations to a post-Trump political landscape. As Bremmer puts it: "Those foreign leaders will start to engage more with the America that they expect to deal with after Trump is gone." Equally significant is his diagnosis of the domestic forces driving this transformation. Economic disillusionment, unfulfilled electoral promises and accusations of political self-interest have, in his assessment, undermined the very coalition that propelled Trump back to the White House. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Greece Approves 10% Crypto Capital Gains Tax as First Framework Lands Below Draft Rate Greece’s parliament approved on Thursday a bill that imposes a 10% capital gains tax on cryptocurrencies, the first comprehensive legal framework for taxing crypto assets in the country. Cryptocurrency capital gains of up to €500 ($563) a year will be exempt from the new tax, the bill says. For bitcoin holders in Greece, that threshold is a small buffer, not a carve-out for larger positions. “Further implementation directives will be published in the coming weeks, which will also define transparency and audit rules,” a senior finance ministry official told Reuters . An earlier draft circulated in October had floated a 15% rate. The version lawmakers passed lands five points lower, while keeping the €500 annual exemption that was already in that proposal. What the levy covers for bitcoin holders The tax is set to apply from Jan. 1, 2027, Greek coverage of the finance ministry bill says. It is levied on the net gain — the difference between the acquisition price and the transfer price — not on the full sale proceeds. Trading fees and other costs tied to the deal can factor into that calculation. A taxable transfer is not limited to selling for euros. Using cryptocurrency to buy goods or services, or contributing it to cover or increase company capital, can also crystallize a gain under the new rules. That matters for anyone in Greece who pays a merchant in bitcoin rather than converting first. Simply holding bitcoin while its euro value rises does not, by itself, create a tax bill. Crypto-to-crypto swaps, such as bitcoin for another token, are treated as non-taxable events in the explanatory material that accompanied the bill, matching the approach France has used to avoid taxing every hop between coins. Net annual gains at or below €500 are exempt. Greek analyses of the text say that once net gains clear that ceiling, the 10% rate applies to the full net gain for the year, not only the slice above €500. Losses above €500 in a tax year may be carried forward for up to five years and offset only against future crypto capital gains. Purchases of crypto assets are also being pulled into Greece’s existing “source of funds” checks from 2027, so buyers may need to show that the euros used to acquire bitcoin or other tokens came from declared income or other lawful capital. The rule does not add a separate purchase tax; it widens the audit trail around how coins were funded. An EU patchwork, not a single rate European Union countries do not share a unified tax system for the sector. Rates on cryptocurrency gains typically run from about 8% to 30% across member states and are usually levied on capital gains, the finance ministry official said. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. He is scheduled to earn $12 million next year, and none of that money is guaranteed," Graziano said. "If he isn't in Baltimore's plans beyond this year, the Ravens could find themselves fielding offers over the next week." Fielding offers isn't the same as shopping a player, but as the math becomes more difficult for the Ravens in the AFC, Graziano lists a handful of reasons why a trade could make sense, from Henry's age and contract to the reality of trying to win without Jackson. The number of contenders in need of a running back could also get the Ravens some value in a trade. Several teams, including the Giants , Broncos , Bengals , Vikings and Packers , have been reported as suitors for Indianapolis' Jonathan Taylor. Only one of them can get him. Could the losers of that sweepstakes make a play for Henry? Teams being interested in Henry is no surprise. The Ravens willingly talking about deals involving Henry is a separate subject, and to this point, no reports have indicated they are looking to deal their running back. With Brissett coming in and a more favorable portion of the schedule ahead, one would think Baltimore still has visions of competing this season. If the Ravens wanted to get something for Henry, though, the best time might be right now. sports.title: Jones - the smiling wind-up artist who refuses to fade away
sports.description: Eddie Jones has coached in Australia, England, Japan and South Africa [Getty Images] An Eddie Jones press conference has always been an event in itself. You never quite know what's coming. A compliment, a cutting observation, a verbal grenade. Sometimes all three, invariably delivered with that mischievous smile. Jones belongs to a disappearing generation of coaches who understood that the contest could begin long before the players took the field. Warren Gatland could intimidate with his imposing presence and gruff demeanour alone. Jose Mourinho proclaimed himself 'The Special One' and made confrontation an art form. Jones was different. Small in stature, with an almost permanent grin, he could stir up an entire nation while thoroughly enjoying himself. All three built reputations on dominance. Not simply on the pitch, but over the agenda, their players and the organisations they represented. But the language of coaching is changing. Wales head coach Steve Tandy talks about connection and relationships. Brighton manager Fabian Hurzeler emphasises collaboration, trust and understanding the person behind the player. Neither lacks ambition or authority, but their approach contrasts with the era of the all-powerful head coach. At 66, Jones remains one of rugby's most fascinating characters from that old school. The method behind the mischief In 2018 Jones questioned whether Wales fly-half Rhys Patchell could handle the pressure of playing England at Twickenham, while describing Warren Gatland's team as "confident and cocky". But his provocations sometimes crossed the line. That same year Jones apologised after footage emerged of him using some choice language to describe Wales and Ireland in less than flattering terms at a sponsors' event the previous year. The former was classic Jones. Identify a weakness, plant a seed of doubt and ensure everyone was talking about it. The latter showed when the wind-ups went too far. But how much was calculated? Speaking to BBC Sport prior to Japan's Nations Championship meeting with Wales, Jones offered an intriguing explanation. "Some of them were planned to an extent. Others might have come out of the press conference. Sometimes you say things at the press conference that you don't mean to say. But, yeah, sometimes." Jones explained that part of his responsibility was to provide that self-belief. "So I felt one of my roles was to give them that confidence, to be almost the battering ram for them." technology.title: Threat actor targets Indian fintechs on weekends when defenders aren’t watching
technology.description: India’s Computer Emergency Response Team has warned the nation’s financial services industry of a “significant escalation” in attacks by what it describes as an “AI-assisted financial threat actor” that has re-targeted victims after they flubbed remediation efforts. CERT-IN first detected the attacks in October and issued advisory in which it warned digital lending platforms, fintech entities, payment service providers, and wallet operators that attackers were targeting internet-facing applications, exposed APIs and privileged endpoints. If the attackers found a way in, they tried to use payment APIs to steal money. On Thursday, the CERT published an update in which it said it continues to hear of successful attacks, including from outfits that tried to remediate their systems after earlier incidents. “The same entities have been deliberately re-targeted, including after incomplete remediation and attacks have been timed to coincide with holidays, weekends and other low-monitoring windows to delay detection and response,” the CERT warned. CERT-IN has decided the attackers need a name and chose “CRAFTY FALCON.” The security org has also revealed that the crew uses AI-enhanced tools including the ARTEX pen-testing tool, the Cairn attack search engine, and the CyberStrikeAI framework – all of which have been linked to users who appear to speak Chinese . CRAFTY FALCON’s tactics see it go looking for internet-exposed environments used for testing or development, where it finds artefacts such as shared credentials, tokens, or network paths that help it move into production systems. If it gets in, the crew re-writes victims’ applications so they do things like make unauthorized API calls. Victims’ defenses assume that only legitimate apps would call those APIs, so activity conducted by the re-written apps aren’t flagged as an attack. Even if victims suspect an attack, they have a lot to cope with because CERT-IN says CRAFTY FALCON creates many “functionally identical variants refined in rapid succession; a pattern consistent with AI-generated code and iterative AI-assisted development.” The crew also quickly exploits newly discovered vulnerabilities to keep its attacks fresh. Once it gets a toehold, the criminal crew makes tiny payments of about $0.01 to test if its attacks work. If those transfers work, CRAFTY FALCON makes larger payments. When the target is a cryptocurrency exchange or virtual digital asset service provider, the crew steals wallet keys and empties cryptocurrency wallets. Vendors of observability tools will be warming up their Indian sales teams today, because CERT-IN’s advice to Indian businesses includes improving their ability to log events, monitor for anomalies in real time, and send alerts. It also urged keeping test environments off the internet, and restricting access to cloud resources because CRAFTY FALCON is fond of using them to run its attacks. technology.title: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
technology.description: Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password. The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine. Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. Alpine is a lightweight, widely used Linux distribution. Other platforms may be affected if they use the same configurations. One connection, works every time, needs no retries There are two other conditions necessary for successful exploitation. First, a system must have at least one user account that’s accessible using a password that is hashed using the SHA256 or SHA512 functions. Second, the target system account must be configured to be passwordless, by way of specifying a "*" in the password field in /etc/shadow, the Linux file where password hashes are stored. Passwordless accounts are commonly used for accounts that use certificate-based authentication. This setting is common for certain types of accounts. Read full article Comments

technology.title: Feds warn grocers: Don't chill on cyber defenses as freezer hacking spree heats up
technology.description: If you have any industrial smart freezers, look out. The US federal government is urging owners and operators to disconnect them from the internet, apply patches, change default passwords, and take other security measures to prevent the kind of attacks that have become prevalent in Europe. “We are seeing these systems targeted across critical infrastructure sectors globally, putting inventory and equipment at risk,” FBI Cyber Branch Operations Director Brett Leatherman said in a statement. Since mid-October, unknown miscreants have hacked thousands of remote-controlled refrigeration systems across hundreds of grocery stores in France, Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg, and Sweden. The attacks increase the temperature inside fridges to highs of 50ºC (122°F), spoiling food, and sparking fires. The Register asked the FBI if it has documented any successful or attempted attacks against refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems in America. We had not received a response to our questions at the time of publication, nor are we aware of any documented digital attacks against these systems in American supermarkets. But there are signs that stateside operators are aware of the issue. Dutch grocery giant Ahold Delhaize, which operates US supermarket chains Food Lion, Giant Food, and Stop & Shop, last month said it proactively took IT systems offline following a cyberattack that affected most of its US and European brands. Delhaize supermarkets in Europe are among those hit by the destructive freezer attacks. The Pentagon is also reportedly treating a series of freezer malfunctions that spoiled food at military bases across the US in August as a suspected cyberattack, according to Reuters, which cited four officials familiar with the matter. In a Thursday advisory, the US FBI, Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Health and Human Services, and departments of Agriculture and Transportation warned organizations about the ongoing cyber threats facing operators of industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems. “The actors may exploit vulnerabilities or weaknesses in unpatched or internet-accessible controllers to remotely alter settings and force units into continuous heating and defrost cycles, which can cause widespread inventory loss and equipment hazards,” the agencies said . Attackers exploit these flaws by bypassing authentication, injecting arbitrary code, and abusing weak configurations, according to the feds. Once criminals gain access to the systems, they can change the temperature to spoil food or temperature-controlled medications, start fires, and ultimately harm people who consume products that haven’t been stored at proper temperatures. How to stay frosty To prevent these scenarios, the government organizations urge owners and operators to “immediately” implement best practices and security protections. It's also the inheritor of Amazon Q Developer coding assistant users, who have been directed to migrate to Kiro . It's also " an AI-powered development environment that helps you build software from prototype to production." It's "available as a desktop IDE, a command-line interface, a web app, a mobile app, and a personal AI agent (Crew)." Except that Kiro Crew is also "the persistent, open source development workspace." It's more agent infrastructure – an environment – that supports Kiro Web , IDE , and CLI . To help get Kiro through its identity crisis and perhaps make it more beloved, AWS is expanding Kiro's remit still further. technology.title: The White House is apparently a popular residential proxy exit spot
technology.description: Whether through malware or other means, devices associated with the White House network appear to be serving as residential proxy exit nodes, potentially posing security risks to one of the world's most sensitive networks. News of the security snafu comes from security firm Layer3 Intel, which reported this week that it discovered the likely illicit activity thanks to its recently launched Residential Proxy Observatory . According to Layer3 founder Sergiy Usatyuk, the White House residential proxy activity might have gone unnoticed if not for the new tool. “The observatory is just a public interface to explore the data we've been collecting for the past year,” Usatyuk told The Register in an email. For those unfamiliar with residential proxies, they're like any old proxy network that obfuscates the location of a user, except in this case their exit nodes use IP addresses associated with residential internet connections, as opposed to datacenters. While many are legitimate, others are exploited by threat actors and used in the commission of cybercrimes, as the FBI warned earlier this year. The FBI bulletin, put out in March, warns users to protect their systems against hijacking via malware, illicit SDK partnerships, VPNs with hidden service terms that repurpose user computers as exit nodes, and other threats used to turn victims into nodes without their consent. Residential proxies are commonly used by threat actors to conceal command-and-control (C2) infrastructure, conduct phishing attacks, send spam, disguise malicious traffic, and the like, the FBI explained. According to Layer3, its data shows 28 distinct residential proxy services exiting into the White House network nearly every day between October 5 and November 3, with 236 separate exits in that period. Other residential proxy detection services logged the same information, Layer3 said. Most of the activity was happening in the evening, White House time, between 5 pm and midnight. That, Layer3 said, suggests someone at the White House - not a guest - has an infected device that’s serving as an exit, likely via an infected proxy SDK. If correct, that’s a problem. “Past research has shown that poorly secured proxy SDKs can allow internal network access and lateral movement,” Layer3 explained. “If an SDK on this network has the same kind of flaw, anyone buying proxy access could use it to reach internal systems.” In other words, this is a serious security risk, and one Usatyuk tells us could have been a problem for a while. “Our data retention period goes back to July 10,” the Layer3 founder explained. “Given that there was continuous activity for a matter of months and other res proxy detection services independently verified the data, it's likely that White House IPs have been used by res proxy networks for all sorts of activity for some time now.” Usatyuk said his firm’s data isn’t detailed enough to know how many machines are being used as exit nodes inside the White House network. technology.title: Software squeezes more data out of Webb Telescope for imaging exoplanets
technology.description: With a huge and still-growing catalog of exoplanets, researchers are eager to take the next steps: trying to infer what conditions are like on them, either by imaging them directly or by capturing the light that has passed through their atmosphere. Both are substantial challenges, given the presence of stars that are far, far brighter than light that has come to us via the planet. While telescopes can be fitted with devices called coronagraphs that block out much of a star's light, there are limits to their effectiveness, caused by noise from subtle variations in the telescope's configuration and pointing between observations. Now, researchers have developed a new software package that optimizes a physical model of the telescope in a way that allows us to better model these differences, producing low-noise imaging of exoplanets. Point spreads Central to this work is the concept of a point spread function. If you use a telescope to image a single point of light, it will not appear that way in the actual image. Instead, it will be slightly blurry and spread out, due to imperfections in the telescope hardware and the limits of our ability to keep it pointed accurately through the time it takes to image something. The mathematical description of how a telescope distorts a point of light is called its point spread function. Read full article Comments

science.title: 'We got it done!' Spacewalking astronauts finish installing next-gen ISS solar arrays
science.description: null Just as NASA is preparing to demonstrate " Max Power " on the ground, two astronauts on a spacewalk have provided the International Space Station (ISS) with the same. Expedition 75 flight engineers Anil Menon of NASA and Joshua Kutryk of the Canadian Space Agency installed and deployed the eighth and final ISS Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) on Thursday (Nov. 5), augmenting the space station's legacy solar array wings to produce as much as 30% more electricity. "We got it done!" said Menon at the end of the 6-hour-and-59-minute spacewalk . The EVA (extravehicular activity) began at 8:36 a.m. EST and ended at 3:35 p.m. EST (1336 to 2035 GMT). NASA astronaut Anil Menon (at far right) is seen at the base of the newly-deployed eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) during a spacewalk on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) Repeating many of the same tasks as they did on an Oct. 29 spacewalk that added the penultimate iROSA, Menon and Kutryk worked this time on the starboard side of the station's backbone truss on the 3B power channel. The two retrieved the 750-pound (340 kilograms) iROSA assembly from a temporary stowage platform, carried it to the worksite by way of the Canadarm2 robotic arm and mounted it to its previously assembled bracket kit. Menon then attached the cables to tie the iROSA into the station's systems but ran into a problem. "We are seeing half of the expected shunt current that we want," radioed Nichole Stilwell, a NASA astronaut serving as the spacewalk officer in Mission Control. "In this current config, we are not necessarily going to deploy." To address the issue, the connectors needed to be inspected. Out of safety concerns — given that the arrays generate electricity whenever lit by the sun — the astronauts needed to wait for the space station to enter the shadow of Earth to see what could be done. In the interim, they spent the time cleaning up their worksite and returning the Canadarm2 to its park site as they would have done after the deployment. Fortunately, they were able to clear the issue. "We are seeing good shunt currents on the ground, so we are go for deploy," said Stilwell. Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk (at center) works on mounting the eighth and final International Space Station Roll-Out Solar Array (iROSA) during a spacewalk on Nov. 5, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) After releasing two bolts, Kutryk and Menon watched as the array started to unfurl to its full 63-foot (19 meters) length. No motor was needed; the iROSA, as designed, used only the potential energy stored by its rolled-up carbon composite booms to extend itself. The entire process took about 10 minutes. "Today marks the completion of not just one solar array but, over 15 years after its development, eight arrays," said Menon at the close of the spacewalk. "These solar arrays are incredible. science.description: null Blue Origin's big rocket is getting a little bigger. Jeff Bezos' company announced today (Nov. 5) that it has developed a third stage for its New Glenn rocket, which it says will make the powerful launcher more capable and flexible. The stage, called the GS3, "enhances New Glenn's capabilities," Blue Origin said in a blog post today . Its reusable first stage is powered by seven of Blue Origin's BE-4 engines, and its second stage features two of the company's BE-3Us. The rocket stands 322 feet (98 meters) tall and can haul 14.3 tons (13 metric tons) to geostationary transfer orbit (GTO) and 50 tons (45 metric tons) to low Earth orbit (LEO). These are the specs for the standard, or "7x2," version of New Glenn. Last year, Blue Origin announced that it's developing a super-heavy variant known as the 9x4, because it will feature nine first-stage BE-4s and four upper-stage BE-3Us. The 9x4 will be nearly 400 feet (122 m) tall, and it will be able to loft 15.4 tons (14 metric tons) to GTO and 77 tons (70 metric tons) to LEO, according to Blue Origin . science.title: The economic benefits of the covid vaccines may be double what we thought
science.description: The covid-19 vaccines were costly to produce, but paid for themselves many times over Paul Christian Gordon / Alamy The covid-19 vaccines may have provided health and economic benefits worth up to $64.3 trillion in the first year alone – almost double an earlier estimate. Previously, researchers calculated that the $79.4 billion invested in developing covid-19 vaccines saw a return of between $4.8 trillion and $37.9 trillion globally in the first 12 months after their rollout. But now, a reanalysis of the data suggests it is actually between $6.43 trillion and $64.3 trillion. This means that for every $1 spent on the vaccines’ development, between $59.70 and $809 was gained in that year. “It is great to finally see this research published to demonstrate the enormous health and financial benefits gained from covid-19 vaccines, in comparison to the costs that went into their development and delivery,” says Hallie Benjamin at the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine. Read more Does each new covid-19 variant pose a significant threat? The $6.43 trillion figure is based on a cost-effectiveness analysis that is generally used in the health sector and factors in quality of life, while the $64.3 trillion figure is based on a cost-benefit analysis used in the public sector. Advertisement Both include data from 173 countries on averted hospitalisations, productivity losses and lives saved. For instance, one of the estimates Benjamin and her colleagues used came from modelling that suggested the vaccines prevented 14 million to 20 million deaths in their first year. The initial $4.8 trillion and $37.9 trillion figures were released when the research was in a preprint stage, before it had been peer-reviewed. “We made many changes throughout the peer-review process that strengthened the quality of our findings,” says Benjamin. The researchers originally used the Value of Statistical Life Years, which considers how many years a person would be likely to live because of the vaccine, a figure that would be lower if someone was older. As part of the peer-review process, they were advised to use the Value of Statistical Life. Team member Mark Jit at New York University says this treats life spans more equally and is aligned with recommendations for valuing mortality-risk reductions. But the returns weren’t equally distributed. The researchers found that the vaccines had the highest returns in richer countries. This was probably because poorer countries accessed them later, so fewer lives were saved and fewer productivity and healthcare costs were averted, says Jit. The results are “a message about the need for being able to distribute the vaccines fairly to the people most in need around the world”, he says. Covid raises risk of heart issues in children

But the history of such use is likely to go back much further. Genomic studies suggest that the domestication of cannabis plants ( Cannabis sativa ) was happening in China about 12,000 years ago , with people potentially exploiting it for oil and hemp fibre. Archaeological sites with artefacts made from hemp dating to 7500 years ago have been found in China and Japan .
